extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, individuals and organizations who want to submit federal public comments (advocates, experts, affected stakeholders)
extracted.subtask_description: Drafting and submitting comments to federal agencies on proposed rules, requests for information, and information-collection activities to influence agency decisionmaking. Covers where to find notices, how to submit, and what content makes a comment effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly state your position
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly state your position (support or opposition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the main stance explicit at the start of the comment so the agency knows whether you support or oppose the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify yourself and explain your connection
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify yourself and explain your connection to the issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain who you are and why the issue matters to you; comments carry more weight when from experts or affected stakeholders. Example phrasing: 'As a parent of a special needs child...'

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay focused on the agency's specific proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Stay focused on the agency's specific proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address the proposal under consideration rather than unrelated policy preferences or tangential topics so the agency can directly use your input on the rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include data, evidence, and statistics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support assertions with empirical information where possible to strengthen the persuasive force and substantiveness of your comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include personal narratives
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use firsthand stories to illustrate how the proposal would affect real people; combine narratives with evidence for maximum impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use specific examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Use specific examples: 'As a parent of a special needs child...'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete examples ground abstract arguments and help agencies understand practical consequences of their decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit comments through regulations.gov (text or document uploads)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public submissions are made through regulations.gov via text entry or document uploads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the official portal when filing comments so they are part of the agency's docket and can be reviewed and considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe comment period deadlines (typically ~60 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments typically remain open for 60 days (longer for certain requests).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File within the published comment period on the Federal Register; some notices specify longer or shorter windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make comments substantive (agencies legally must consider substantive comments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must legally consider all substantive comments before finalizing rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide substantive, on-point reasoning and evidence rather than slogans or off-topic remarks so the agency is required to consider and respond to your points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand which item type you're commenting on
rubrics_metrics.description: Three types of items open to comment: Rules; Requests for Information; Information Collection Activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor your comment to the item type: rulemakings concern regulatory text/requirements; RFIs solicit expertise; information-collection activities weigh data needs against respondent burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find notices in the Federal Register
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies publish notices in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor the Federal Register to learn what is open for comment and to find details like deadlines, docket numbers, and submission instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware agencies group comments by topic and campaign
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies review and group comments by topic and campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may aggregate similar comments when analyzing input; providing distinct, substantive points can help ensure your specific concerns are visible within grouped submissions.
